text:
ida_ml: quick question — for per-customer SLO mapping, are we comfortable using FP8 by default on non‑PII endpoints? seeing variance spikes on longctx generation :thinking:

matt_p: what's the SLO we care about here? latency or quality budget?

ida_ml: quality first for these customers, target is <1.5% QA regression vs fp32 on our eval suite, latency goal is <= 1.2x baseline.

kim_ops: if we roll FP8 we need clear rollback hooks and an eval holdout per customer. also add alerting for degscore and user-facing error rate :eyes:

liam_infra: runtime supports per-request precision selection, can route by customer flag. cost delta for FP8 vs INT8 looks ~25% savings across typical token distributions.

ida_ml: here's a tiny sketch of the runtime config I had in mind:
```
quant_profiles:
  - name: fp8_aggressive
    allowed: [fp8, int8, fp32]
    selection_policy: per_customer_slo
    quality_threshold: 0.985  # relative to fp32
```

matt_p: nice. we should also measure variance (stddev) of LM logprobs across prompts, not just mean perplexity. FP8 sometimes has heavy tails on rare tokens.

eval-bot: eval summary (holdout set): FP8 -> +1.8% QA error, INT8 -> +0.6% QA error; FP8 tail token stddev +27% vs fp32; latency +8%

kim_ops: then FP8 default feels risky for strict-quality customers. suggest canary: 1% traffic -> 5% -> 20% with automatic rollback if QA_error > 1.2% or tail_stddev > 15%

liam_infra: agree. can implement canary gating in routing layer and emit these extra telemetry fields: quant_profile, tail_stddev, qa_delta, per-token-loss-histogram.

ida_ml: action items: (1) add telemetry keys (kim/liam), (2) create per-customer holdouts and define quality SLAs (matt/ida), (3) implement canary gating + automatic rollback (liam/ops). I'll draft the RFC follow-up with measured thresholds.

matt_p: and add cost/latency accounting per-profile so product can decide pricing/tiers :chart_with_upwards_trend:

kim_ops: will set up alert runbook for rollbacks. thanks — keeping this small and staged makes sense.

ida_ml: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
